playbook.intent: Someone is holding an opportunity hypothesis with nothing behind it yet but a hunch that a particular audience would pay for it. It is finished when the smallest version that exercises the whole chain end to end is live for real users and the metrics chosen up front are reporting numbers against it.
playbook.scope: From an opportunity hypothesis through evidence-backed problem framing, MVP scoping, build, launch, and first iteration. Ends when MVP is in production with success metrics tracked.

success-criteria.criterion: The opportunity is stated in one paragraph a stranger can read: the outcome wanted, the constraints it lives under, and the condition that would end the effort
The job the target segment is hiring this product to do is named from interview quotes and usage evidence, not from what the team assumed at the outset
A story map shows the slice chosen for the first release and, in the same picture, what was deliberately cut out of it
One end-to-end path can be completed by a user without anyone stepping in manually behind the scenes
Success metrics carry target numbers and are wired into analytics before launch rather than reconstructed afterwards
The release reached its intended audience with the rollback path and the instrumentation both proven against live traffic
A go, iterate or kill call for the next round is written down together with the evidence that produced it

stage.intent: State the outcome, constraints, and exit-condition in one paragraph.
